report.summary: Recognizable and charming: the low stepped red-brick massing, pale flat roofs, narrow north wing, broad post-supported canopy, blue-green entrance, and mostly blank service elevations form a coherent miniature caricature. No obvious visible defects undermine the silhouette or identity.

orientation.summary: The map defines +u as the north-facing side. Located SV1, north of the building and looking SSE, shows the characteristic blue-green principal doors beneath the canopy; the labeled +u render reproduces that entrance. The actual inventory contains one double door on +u and only a single secondary door on west-facing -v, so there is no duplicated principal portal. SV4 and the -v render are consistent with a mostly blank west service wall. This conclusion comes from the located views and face labels, not the nearer south road.

scene_review.summary: The low stepped brick silhouette, pale flat roofs, projecting north wing, slender-post canopy, and blue-green entry form a clear bank miniature. Brick, glazing, and roof treatments remain coherent with neighboring buildings, with no conspicuous rendering defects.

orientation.summary: Independent face findings place the principal entrance on +u/N, and the actual inventory confirms one blue-green double door on that face beneath the canopy. The separate -v/W single service door does not read as a competing principal entrance; the south and east elevations remain appropriately doorless.
